dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatcha up to, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Just keeping an eye on things... Looking out for any problems that might need me to step in.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey, you three. What are you doing here? There should be at least one of you manning the booth at all times.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Accessing booth operation logs... Analyzing... Neb left to try and buy a new blueprint. Ati soon followed to try and stop him. Finally, Raya came to mediate between them.

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: I keep telling you, we don't have that much Mora to spare.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: I just wanted to have a look, what's wrong with that?

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Guys, seriously. Stop fighting...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Here's the thing, Neb. Even if you could afford to buy a blueprint, I'm afraid I couldn't allow it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I know you like building stuff, but these designs aren't for toys like the kind you're used to — they're for weapons which are very complicated to build, and extremely dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: That's a load of baloney, dumpster-diver! My designs are toys too, actually!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh? You build a machine that can blast monsters into the sky, and in your mind that's a toy?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I mean, at the end of the day, is there really that much difference between weapons and toys anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Not where Knuckle Duckle's concerned, that's for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ugh, that's not the point... Anyway, you there with the brown hair. You want a blueprint?

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Yeah... I wanna make some Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots too! I also have some design ideas of my own, and with your bots as the basis, maybe I'll be able to try them out for real...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I get it. Your head's so full of ideas you wanna bring to life that you can hardly sleep at night. You try eating some snacks to take your mind off things, but it doesn't seem to help anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Exactly! Exactly! ...But what can I do? I'll never be able to afford one of your blueprints.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, you must have blueprints for the toys you've made too, right? Let's trade. One of your toys for one of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Really? Thank you so much, Ma'am...? Is it Ma'am, or...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: It's Boss. Boss of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop!

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, Boss of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh, that was very thoughtful. Who are you, and what have you done with Aino?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: What's that supposed to mean? I'm a boss, aren't I? A lot of people depend on me. Looking out for them is a big part of the job.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did that really just happen? For a moment there, Aino stopped being a little kid, and acted like a full-on grown-up. ...A grown-up who's shorter than the kids she was looking out for, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Previous records indicate that Aino has a 94% chance of adopting such behaviors when encountering a child in a similar situation to herself.
